title: Laredo Man Pleads Guilty to Making Machine Gun Used to Kill Alabama Officer
excerpt: Hector Alonzo, 48, of Laredo pleaded guilty in federal court to conspiring to use a machine gun in a marijuana trafficking scheme, admitting he converted a stolen Glock 17 that was later used to kill Huntsville Police Officer Billy Clardy III.
content:
A 48-year-old Laredo man has pleaded guilty in federal court to conspiring to use a machine gun in a marijuana trafficking scheme, after making a weapon that was later used to kill an Alabama police officer, according to the U.S. Department of Justice.

Hector Alonzo pleaded guilty Thursday, Nov. 19. As part of the plea, he admitted to converting a stolen Glock 17 into a machine gun that was used in a drug conspiracy. The investigation revealed Alonzo supplied the weapon and marijuana to LaJeromeny Brown for transport to Tennessee.

On Dec. 6, 2019, Brown planned to deliver 100 pounds of marijuana to a Huntsville, Alabama, residence. As authorities attempted an arrest, Brown used the converted weapon Alonzo made to fatally shoot Huntsville Police Officer Billy Clardy III.

Brown, 48, of Chattanooga, Tennessee, was convicted of capital murder in Alabama and sentenced to death. His sentence was affirmed in August 2026 by the Alabama Court of Criminal Appeals. Co-conspirator Juan Mendoza, 45, of Eagle Pass, pleaded guilty to his role in the scheme on Feb. 3, 2025, and is awaiting sentencing.

Alonzo will be sentenced at a later date. At that time, he faces up to life in federal prison as well as a possible $250,000 fine. The Drug Enforcement Administration, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and the Huntsville Police Department conducted the investigation.

Sources: U.S. Department of Justice, Southern District of Texas, Nov. 19, 2026; KGNS, Nov. 20, 2026.
